Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up: GPU, TPS targets, concurrency, token mix

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what I captured and a few follow-ups so we can put together a Dedicated sizing + quote: 

Summary of requirements (from your team):
- Target endpoints: 3 production endpoints (Chat assist, Summarization, Retrieval-augmented generation)
- Expected average TPS: 150 TPS aggregate across endpoints during peak hour
- Peak concurrency: ~120 simultaneous sessions, average session = 15 reqs/min
- Token mix: ~70% short prompts (<= 64 in), 30% long responses (avg 512 tokens out) — see attached FinCo_token_profile.csv
- Performance SLOs: p95 latency <= 250ms for chat (generation tail), p50 << 100ms for embeddings/short calls
- Model preference: open-model family (LLaMA 2 variants) with 8k context; willing to consider quantized variants for cost savings
- Data/security: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering (not fully on-prem) — want customer-managed keys later in PO

Open questions / asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm the 150 TPS is per-second sustained at peak or bursts? We interpreted as sustained for 10–15 minute windows.
2) Confirm expected percent of requests that require full KV-cache usage (long context) vs short prompt-only. That impacts KV RAM needs.
3) Any flexibility on model latency vs cost (e.g., H100 vs A100 choices)? Rafael will propose hardware permutations.

Next steps:
- Rafael to share a couple of GPU-config sizing options (H100 vs A100, node counts) and estimated throughput/cost.
- I'll assemble a scoped Dedicated quote and draft PO terms.
- Could we schedule a 30m follow-up next week to review sizing and walk through canaries?

Attachments: capacity_estimate_template.xlsx, FinCo_token_profile.csv

Thanks —
Marissa

- KV/cache usage: around 40% of chat requests will need full context (we have long-form conversation history for account support flows).
- Model flexibility: cost is important, but we need to keep p95 under 300ms for generation. We are open to A100 if H100 price delta is significant.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-06-23T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: sizing options for FinTech Co (H100 vs A100)

Marissa / Aditya —

Putting together two realistic configurations based on Sam's clarifications (150 TPS sustained, 20-min peaks, ~40% full-KV). Rough back-of-envelope below — detailed calc in capacity_estimate_template.xlsx: 

Option A — Cost-optimised (A100 80GB):
- Nodes: 6 x A100-80GB (each node = 1 GPU for our dedicated pod topology)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~25–30 TPS per GPU for generation with 8k context quantized fp16; with 6 nodes that's ~150–180 TPS sustainable with batching and KV caching tuned
- KV RAM: plan for ~1.5TB aggregate KV across nodes (replication factor 1 for dedicated, sharded), fits on host RAM with 6 nodes
- Latency: p95 estimated ~220–320ms depending on request length (long responses push toward upper bound)
- Pros: significantly lower monthly cost vs H100; familiar software stack
- Cons: limited headroom for burst growth; longer tail latency on long-context runs

Option B — Performance-first (H100 80GB or L4/H100 mix):
- Nodes: 4 x H100-80GB + 2 x A100 as spillover (or 6 x H100 if budget allows)
- Expected throughput: ~40–45 TPS per H100 for large-gen workloads; with 4 H100 = 160–180 TPS baseline with much better tail latency
- Latency: p95 ~150–220ms
- Pros: headroom for bursts, better tail; simpler autoscaling target
- Cons: material cost delta (H100 pricing is ~30–50% higher depending on supply)

Concurrency / Batching notes:
- With 120 simultaneous sessions and 15 reqs/min avg per session, we should size for ~120 concurrent token-generation contexts. Continuous batching and prefix caching will reduce per-token cost.
- Recommend enabling per-tenant KV caching for sessions that are chat-heavy — reduces repeated decode cost by ~30% in our benchmarks.

Recommendation: start with Option A (6x A100) if FinTech wants to optimize cost and can tolerate occasional tail hits; move to Option B if they prioritize consistent p95 < 250ms and aggressive growth in months 1–6.

I'll prepare a more formal throughput/cost table and a recommended canary rollout (start with 2 nodes traffic split 25% -> scale to 6).

—Rafael
